S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.

subtypes.Feeling Keyed Up: Feeling anxious and wound up like a spring, unable to stay still.
subtypes.Physical Tension: The entire body feels stiff and tense, unable to relax.
subtypes.Nervousness: Nerves are on edge, being startled easily by minor sounds or stimuli.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in the number of arguments with spouse (e.g., either a lot more or a lot less than usual regarding child rearing, personal habits)
patient_info.stressor: During a high-pressure cloud migration at work, Terrell and his wife began arguing far more often about his skipped meals, unfinished home projects, late-night code reviews, and how much time he spent training or mentoring outside the house. What began as conflict about schedules gradually became nine months of pervasive worry about his marriage, job security, finances, household responsibilities, and whether he was failing the standards he set for himself. The worry became hard for him to shut off, disrupted his sleep, left him tense even during CrossFit and chess club, and noticeably impaired his concentration in sprint planning and code reviews. He entered psychiatric care after a tense performance review, when his manager documented missed architectural details and Terrell himself requested help through his employee assistance program.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie in bed exhausted but my brain keeps running through work risks, money, and what I said to my wife, and even when I do fall asleep I wake up around 3 or 4 and can't get back down because I'm already rehearsing tomorrow's problems.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: I came in because I can't stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I'm slipping at work, bills, the house projects I keep dropping, and whether I'm basically failing as a husband and father.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Even when I tell myself to just focus on the code in front of me or breathe through a workout, one concern hooks another until I'm twenty steps ahead imagining a bad review turning into losing my job and my family being worse off because of me.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.
S058.manifestation: I feel wound tight almost all day, like my shoulders are locked up and I'm bracing for something, and I catch myself pacing between meetings or tapping pieces at chess club because sitting still feels impossible.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: During sprint planning or code reviews, I read the same design note three or four times and still miss details because part of my mind is off calculating what I forgot at home or how badly the next argument is going to go.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My manager has started documenting missed architectural details, and at home I’m leaving projects half-finished and showing up distracted enough that the arguments keep escalating.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, since the cloud migration ramped up and the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing.
